item: Per-platform durability: universal ordering contract (bytes stable before visible; everything stable before journaled; journaled stable before printed); macOS/Linux per-file fsync + two device barriers; Windows per-file write-through including write-through renames, no barrier claimed, no invented constants

item: Ingest protocol amendment (concrete-defect standard): stage+fsync all objects, ONE device barrier, THEN rename into place, then journal append+fsync, second barrier, print — no object appears at its hash name before its bytes are on stable media; barrier count and measured constants unchanged
reason: prosecutor:subtractive's constructed input: under the old per-object stage-sync-rename order, power loss could leave a crash-torn object at its final name; a re-run adopted it by presence and printed a snapshot claiming it — falsifying printed=>durable and routing an uncurable condition to exit 3. Amends the round-1 decided protocol; not a reversal.

item: Presence-skip doctrine made consistent: presence gates WRITES (true post-amendment: presence implies bytes reached stable media; every read rehashes so wrong bytes at a right name are loud); presence never answers an integrity question — the membership probe reads
reason: prosecutor:subtractive's asymmetry finding (same inference doctrine in one paragraph, heresy in the next); closed by the protocol amendment plus one consistent rule stated on the surface.

T4 is answered at zero flags by writes-skipped-never-reads. Re-litigation requires a named new defect or brief item plus a skip mechanism that verifies rather than asserts.
